clue.text: As out of date as some of Mrs Ewing's stories

definitions.meaning: behind the times, no longer in fashion
Juliana Horatia Ewing, the Victorian children's author

explanation.surface: Victorian children's tales dismissed as hopelessly dated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something behind the times is antiquated, and Mrs Ewing's collection carries the same word in its title.

clue.text: Shakespeare's wrestler alternatively to alight on love

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
to land is to come down, to alight
love is nil in tennis, the shape of O

explanation.surface: Advice to come down on love as an alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: In As You Like It, the hero wrestles Charles the duke's wrestler.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of As You Like It defeats the wrestler Charles, so he is Shakespeare's grappler.

clue.text: "Frank Churchill … most — occupied about her spectacles" (Jane Austen)

definitions.text: "Frank Churchill … most — occupied about her spectacles" (Jane Austen)

parts.words: "Frank Churchill … most — occupied about her spectacles" (Jane Austen)
parts.note: a quotation from Emma with an adverb missing that means busily or industriously

explanation.surface: A line from Emma about Frank Churchill fussing with Mrs Bates's glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing adverb means in an industrious, busily active manner, describing Frank's attention to the spectacles.

clue.text: Symbolical content of one small ego, richly augmented

explanation.surface: Describing something emblematic in a puffed-up but petty ego.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content of' points inside 'small ego, richly', where the answer runs across the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A work that conveys meaning through figures and emblems is representational in a figurative way.

clue.text: Footballing skill mentioned for Ibsen heroine

indicators.note: mentioned says the football word is spoken, giving a name that sounds alike

parts.note: a header is striking the ball with the head in football

explanation.surface: A football move whose name recalls an Ibsen character.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken in a non-rhotic British accent, the football term matches Ibsen's Hedda Gabler.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedda Gabler is the title character of Ibsen's play, so she is an example of his heroines.

clue.text: Zero allowance, though food for thought in Cicero's performance

parts.note: O looks like the figure zero
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: Cicero delivering food for thought despite no allowance of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'food for thought' plays on a ration as food, but it is part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero was famed for formal speeches, so his performance is a public speech.

clue.text: Metier I arranged for those honourably discharged

indicators.note: arranged means set in a new order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Retired professionals finding a new line of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges METIERI, the letters of 'Metier I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Retired professors keep their title honorifically, released from duty with honour.

clue.text: Nature of autobiography (especially Rousseau's)

parts.note: Rousseau's autobiography is called the Confessions, so its character is that of an admission

explanation.surface: A note on the self-revealing character of Rousseau's memoir.
explanation.definitionFit: Autobiography often reveals private faults, and Rousseau titled his memoir after the admissions it made.

clue.text: Instruction to lubricate one of Mrs Ewing's prime assets?

definitions.meaning: a command to grease something thoroughly: give it plenty of lubricant

definitions.text: one of Mrs Ewing's prime assets
definitions.meaning: the Ewings of the TV soap Dallas made their fortune from Texas petroleum

explanation.surface: A maintenance tip about keeping Mrs Ewing's best property running smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: After 1-across, Mrs Ewing seems to be the Victorian author again; here she is a matriarch of the Ewing oil dynasty in the American soap Dallas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ewing family wealth in Dallas came from drilling for crude, so a gusher is a prime asset.

clue.text: Wycherley produced a plain example of the class. Others may be double

parts.words: Wycherley produced a plain example of the class. Others may be double
parts.note: Wycherley's comedy is The Plain ___ and Congreve's is The Double ___, so the class is people who trade, honestly or otherwise

explanation.surface: A remark on Restoration comedy and its stock characters, plain and double.
explanation.definitionFit: Traders in goods or cards form the class; plain and double are the adjectives in two Restoration play titles.

clue.text: Dickensian lawyer introduces reported strong man to Brutish nitwit

indicators.note: reported says the strongman's name is spoken, giving a name sounding the same

parts.note: Samson is the biblical strong man
BR is the abbreviation for British; the clue's spelling stretches it to a brutish-looking word
an ass is a fool, a nitwit

explanation.surface: A Dickens lawyer bringing a muscleman to meet a brutish fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Sampson Brass is the rascally attorney in The Old Curiosity Shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Sampson Brass is the crooked attorney in Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop, so he is a Dickensian solicitor.

clue.text: Albee's discovery of a newspaper on stage?

definitions.text: Albee's discovery of a newspaper on stage?

parts.words: Albee's discovery of a newspaper on stage?
parts.note: Edward Albee wrote a play called ___ the Sun, and the Sun is also a British newspaper, so the title reads as discovering a paper

explanation.surface: A theatre critic wondering whether Albee's play is about a newspaper turning up on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A discovery is something come upon, and the word for it begins the title of Albee's play about the Sun.

clue.text: Is man I'm reforming offering a belief in vital force?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man rebuilding himself is offering a creed of life force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforming' rearranges ISMANIM, the letters of 'Is man I'm'.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctrine that a soul or spirit animates all things, living or not, is a belief in a vital principle.

clue.text: Baldwin told it of a marriage

definitions.text: Baldwin told it of a marriage

parts.words: Baldwin told it of a marriage
parts.note: a novelist named Baldwin narrated a tale about a marriage; what one tells is a narrative

explanation.surface: A novelist recounting the history of a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: What an author tells is a tale or narrative, here one about a married couple.

clue.text: Classic tremors recorded by writers like Burns and Blake

parts.note: classical antiquity is Greek and Roman, so classic stands for Roman
tics are involuntary twitches or tremors

explanation.surface: Literary history noting shaky verse recorded by Burns and Blake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classic' suggests the opposite literary camp; it gives ROMAN, of ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Burns and Blake are poets of the movement that followed the Augustans, valuing feeling and nature.

clue.text: The —, and 'well as we are 'people " (Sydney Smith)

definitions.text: The —, and 'well as we are 'people " (Sydney Smith)

parts.words: The —, and 'well as we are 'people " (Sydney Smith)
parts.note: a quotation from Sydney Smith about people who cling to old error, those happy as they are

explanation.surface: A garbled Sydney Smith quotation about complacent people content as they are.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an obstinate adherence to a customary error, as in Sydney Smith's attack on complacent people.

clue.text: Dalmatian resort area opened up by Italians

definitions.text: Dalmatian resort area opened up by Italians

parts.words: Dalmatian resort area opened up by Italians
parts.note: the Adriatic coast of Dalmatia was conquered and organised as a province by the Romans, the Italians of antiquity

explanation.surface: A travel note on a holiday coast in Dalmatia developed by Italian investors.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman province on the eastern Adriatic included the Dalmatian coast that Rome opened up.

clue.text: Burns showed him with a book

definitions.text: Burns showed him with a book

parts.words: Burns showed him with a book
parts.note: a match is a light that burns, and Burns the poet wrote of the Devil, here one keeping a book of sins

explanation.surface: A portrait by Robert Burns of a figure holding a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burns' is the poet, and also what a match does; a book of matches holds this old name for a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The fallen angel is the Devil, and the name also meant a friction match, which comes in a book.

clue.text: New hoard in school of Hellenistic sculpture

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters of the next two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newly found hoard in a school of Greek sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges HOARDIN, the letters of 'hoard in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The sculptors of the island of Rhodes, makers of the Laocoon, formed a Hellenistic school.

clue.text: Author seen to be as new after a brawl

indicators.note: after says the letter for new follows the fight

parts.note: a fray is a noisy fight or brawl

explanation.surface: A writer looking as good as new after a scuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Frayn is the English novelist and playwright of Noises Off.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Frayn is a British novelist and playwright, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Intended murder victim fortuitously can flee

explanation.surface: A marked man who by luck manages to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fortuitously' rearranges CANFLEE, the letters of 'can flee'; Banquo's son escapes Macbeth's murderers.
explanation.definitionFit: Banquo's son in Macbeth is targeted along with his father but escapes the murderers.

clue.text: Part of play on eternity for unlucky hunter

parts.note: an act is a division of a play
an aeon is an immensely long time, an eternity

explanation.surface: A playwright's piece set on eternity about a luckless huntsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth he saw Artemis bathing and was turned into a stag and killed by his own hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical huntsman who saw Artemis bathing was turned into a stag and torn apart by his hounds.

clue.text: American money, we hear, for British poet

explanation.surface: A pun on American small change and an English versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Nichols was an English poet of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Nichols was an English war poet, an example of a British writer of verse.

clue.text: Musical direction from some loose guesswork

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Picking a musical instruction by vague guessing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian instruction tells the performer to continue straight on into the next section without a break.

clue.text: Like Keats's unheard melodies

explanation.surface: A comparison with the silent music on Keats's Grecian urn.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats calls unheard melodies more delightful than heard ones, using the comparative of a word for pleasing.

clue.text: Children's writer frequently seen in the heather

indicators.note: seen in places the word for often inside the plant

parts.note: ling is a common name for heather
oft is an old word for often, frequently

explanation.surface: A children's author often spotted out on the moors.
explanation.walkthrough: Hugh Lofting wrote the Doctor Dolittle books.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh Lofting created Doctor Dolittle, so he is an example of an author for children.

clue.text: Sun item rewritten for dancers

definitions.note: the definition reads as pieces of music written for dancers to perform to

indicators.note: rewritten means written out again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tabloid piece reworked for an audience of dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' rearranges SUNITEM, the letters of 'Sun item'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stately French court dances in three-four time are compositions intended for people to step to.

clue.text: Shelley's doctor

explanation.surface: A question about which physician Shelley consulted.
explanation.walkthrough: Shelley suggests Percy; it is Mary Shelley, whose scientist hero gives her novel its title.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Shelley's Victor, a scientist who animates a creature, is the doctor of her novel.
